label: TP-Link EAP615-Wall
description: AX1800 wall-plate Wi-Fi 6 access point: one gigabit uplink (PoE in), three gigabit downlinks with a 12 W PoE passthrough on one, dual-band 802.11ax. The passthrough port is a PSE only while the uplink is fed 802.3at; on 802.3af the AP runs and the passthrough jack stays dark.
notes: Vendor figures from the TP-Link page for the US model, https://www.tp-link.com/us/business-networking/omada-sdn-access-point/eap615-wall/v1/ (HTTP 200, 230,762 B, read 2026-11-21): Interface - "Uplink: 1x 10/100/1000 Mbps Ethernet Port / Downlink: 3x 10/100/1000 Mbps Ethernet Ports (One port supports PoE OUT. The PoE OUT feature requires 802.3at PoE+ input. The maximum power output for POE pass-through is 13 W (EU version) or 12 W (US version), based on laboratory testing.)"; Max. Power Consumption - "EU: 10W (802.3at PoE, PoE Out off) / US: 11.5W (802.3at PoE, PoE Out off)". The 12 W modelled is the US figure because this spec is sourced from the /us/ page; the EU unit is 13 W. Radios are AX1800 - 574M on 2.4 GHz and 1.2G on 5 GHz - the 2x2 Wi-Fi 6 split for that class. The uplink keeps the 12.95 W 802.3af class-3 allowance, which covers the 11.5 W the AP draws with the passthrough off. The passthrough's 802.3at precondition is not expressible in the spec schema today - `poe.budgetW` is unconditional - which the poe note says outright.

poe.note: 12 W, the US unit's stated maximum passthrough output ("The maximum power output for POE pass-through is 13 W (EU version) or 12 W (US version), based on laboratory testing."). One PSE port, so the device total is the port ceiling. The vendor makes the figure conditional twice over: the passthrough exists only when an 802.3at port feeds the AP - an 802.3af uplink powers the 11.5 W radio and leaves this jack dead - and 12 W is a laboratory maximum, not a standard class. The schema has no field for "this PSE is conditional on the input", so an AP fed from an 802.3af port still shows eth3 allocating 12 W in `show power inline`; the condition is recorded here and in the description until a field exists to gate it.
